slides.title: Same Method, Different Task: What the Bitter Lesson Does Not License in Social Simulation
slides.tldr: Bitter lesson limits in social simulation
slides.highlight: This paper argues that the 'bitter lesson' does not justify replacing hand-built agents with LLMs in social simulation because prediction lacks the stakes required for cooperation and norm enforcement, a distinction critical for MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: LLM social simulations fail because prediction lacks stakes, violating the Bitter Lesson's same-task condition.
card.key_idea: Substituting hand-built agents with LLMs violates the Bitter Lesson; prediction is solitary, lacking the 'stakes' required for cooperation.
card.evaluation: 540-agent pilot in common-pool resource game; persistent stakes altered strategies but failed to produce human-like heterogeneity.
card.limitation: Environment lacked genuine payoff externalities, preventing a definitive test of whether stakes alone generate interested-party behavior.

slides.title: Scientific Liquidity Agents: An Agent-Based Model of Knowledge Arbitrage in Scientific Communities
slides.tldr: AGENT-BASED MODEL OF SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE ARBITRAGE
slides.highlight: This work introduces an agent-based model for simulating knowledge arbitrage and liquidity in scientific communities, offering a process-oriented framework for analyzing how specialized knowledge moves between research contexts.

card.one_liner: Agent-based model simulates knowledge arbitrage, revealing verification bottlenecks despite abundant scientific production.
card.key_idea: Combines domain specialists and epistemic arbitrageurs in a shared environment with problem graphs, interaction networks, and publication registries.
card.evaluation: Two exploratory simulations (10 and 18 agents) analyzed via contact pairs, solved problems, and replication outcomes; lacks external baselines.
card.limitation: Highly stylized synthetic environment with small agent counts; replication failures may reflect model rules rather than real-world dynamics.

slides.title: Just Between Us? Exploring a Wearable-Mediated Channel for Discreet Human-Agent Interaction in a Shared Game Setting
slides.highlight: This study explores a wearable-mediated channel combining in-ear audio and head tilts for discreet human-agent interaction in shared settings, addressing the need for private communication in embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Wearable-mediated discreet interaction enables private agent-human communication in shared games without increasing wearer stress.
card.key_idea: Combines in-ear audio for agent messages with head-tilt detection for responses, facilitating private bidirectional exchange in multi-party settings.
card.evaluation: Wizard-of-Oz study with 40 participants in a card game; measured protocol consistency, wearer stress, usability, and non-wearer awareness.
card.limitation: Formative study using a controlled game; results may not generalize to complex real-world social dynamics or autonomous agents.

slides.title: When Debate Amplifies Risk: Social-Bias Vulnerabilities in Multi-Agent Safety Deliberation
slides.tldr: SOCIAL BIAS AMPLIFIES SAFETY RISKS IN MULTI-AGENT DEBATE
slides.highlight: This paper demonstrates how social biases like conformity and authority deference can cause multi-agent debate systems to catastrophically amplify safety risks, offering an inference-time auditing framework to mitigate these vulnerabilities. It is relevant to MIMIC for understanding how interpersonal dynamics in hybrid human-AI societies can override evidence-grounded safety boundaries in collaborative agent models.

card.one_liner: Multi-agent debate amplifies web safety risks via social bias; RiskTrace-Debias mitigates this with inference-time auditing.
card.key_idea: SafeConflict-Bias isolates social cues; RiskTrace-Debias uses evidence precommitment, metadata masking, and consistency gating to enforce safety.
card.evaluation: Tested on 700 instances across four LLMs; reduced unsafe adoption from 100% to ≤2% without over-refusal, validated via ablations.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate initial evidence categorization; may suppress valid minority dissent if anchor formulation is flawed.

slides.title: Xinhua Unveils Bionic Humanoid Robot News Anchors with UBTECH
slides.highlight: The deployment of bionic humanoid robots as news anchors demonstrates real-world applications of embodied agents in public-facing roles, offering insights into human-robot interaction dynamics relevant to social robotics.

slides.title: UK Insurance Policy Launched for Domestic Humanoid Robot Injuries
slides.highlight: The launch of an insurance policy for domestic humanoid robot injuries in the UK highlights emerging regulatory and liability frameworks for home-based embodied AI, a key consideration for the deployment of social robots like Haru.

slides.title: Selective, Risk-Controlled Emotion Forecasting in Conversation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a risk-controlled framework for forecasting emotional departures in conversation using conformal guarantees, which aligns with HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception by providing calibrated uncertainty estimates for dynamic human-AI interaction states.

card.one_liner: Emotion forecasting should predict state changes, not values, using conformal risk control for reliable selective commitment.
card.key_idea: Reframes forecasting to detect departures from persistence using selective commitment policies and dialogue-level conformal risk control.
card.evaluation: Tested on IEMOCAP, DailyDialog, MELD, EmoryNLP via CCC, AUPRC, LT-F1; verified risk guarantees across 12 configurations.
card.limitation: Persistence barrier relies on oracle historical states; risk control incurs high abstention rates, reducing recall significantly.

slides.title: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
slides.highlight: This paper introduces an open smart-ring platform that integrates speech, gesture, and physiological sensing to control robots, offering a wearable interface model relevant to embodied human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: OpenZilo is an open smart-ring platform enabling human-centric robot interaction via speech, gestures, and physiological sensing.
card.key_idea: Integrates microphone, IMU, PPG, and temperature sensors with a modular software architecture separating acquisition, event interpretation, policy, and robot execution.
card.evaluation: Tested with 10 participants on Unitree robots; achieved ~90% task success for speech/gestures and compared response times against human baselines.
card.limitation: Small convenience sample, simulated physiological events, and lack of statistical significance tests limit generalizability and real-world validation.

slides.title: Must AI Spell It Out? Pragmatic Comprehension of Alerts in a Time-Critical Task
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that users can effectively interpret underspecified alerts from AI systems by leveraging prior knowledge, supporting the development of more efficient, human-like communication strategies in assistive contexts.

card.one_liner: Pragmatic AI assistants improve time-critical monitoring by leveraging user prior knowledge to shorten alerts.
card.key_idea: An RSA-based planner adapts alert specificity to user knowledge, saving time for subsequent critical events in dynamic environments.
card.evaluation: Preregistered study (N=114) in DroneWorld compared pragmatic vs. baseline assistants; pragmatic group detected more problems faster with lower mental load.
card.limitation: Benefit concentrated in low-awareness scenes; high-awareness users saw no significant detection improvement over fully specified baselines.

slides.title: Mediating Human-Swarm Interactions Through a Robot Helper: A Shepherding-Inspired Approach
slides.highlight: This study explores human-swarm interaction using an intermediary robot helper to steer ungovernable collectives, offering insights into managing hybrid group dynamics through motion primitives.

card.one_liner: Motion-primitives outperform teleoperation in steering swarms, reducing workload and improving task performance.
card.key_idea: Compares continuous teleoperation against shepherding-inspired motion primitives (flank, drive, stop) that autonomously navigate relative to swarm convex hulls.
card.evaluation: VR study with 24 participants using Boids simulation; measured penned boid count and NASA-TLX workload across low/high cohesion scenarios.
card.limitation: Relies on simulated Boids dynamics; real-world swarms may exhibit complex behaviors not captured by simple local interaction rules.

slides.title: User Attributes and Political Ideology Shape LLM Receptiveness in Online Political Debates
slides.highlight: This study reveals that LLMs exhibit systematic receptiveness asymmetries based on user political ideology and expertise, which is critical for HyECHO's goal of modeling fair and accurate social perception in hybrid human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: LLMs systematically favor left-leaning users in political debates, regardless of stance or expertise.
card.key_idea: Reconstructed Debate.org and controlled multi-turn simulations isolate user attributes, revealing persistent ideological bias in LLM receptiveness.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 150k conversations across four models using Debate.org and Political Compass Test data, validated by human annotators and logistic regressions.
card.limitation: Bias is not fixed; fine-tuning on different political corpora can erase or reverse the observed ideological asymmetry.

slides.title: VIPBench: A Human-Aligned Benchmark for Voice Identity Perception in the Age of Voice Cloning
slides.tldr: BENCHMARKING HUMAN VS MODEL VOICE IDENTITY PERCEPTION
slides.highlight: VIPBench evaluates how human listeners perceive voice identity across real, cloned, and morphed speech, revealing significant divergences between model similarity scores and human judgments. This is relevant to HyECHO for understanding the limitations of current speaker representations in modeling human-perceived identity within hybrid human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: VIPBench evaluates voice identity models against human perception, revealing significant divergence from metadata labels for AI clones.
card.key_idea: A benchmark of 124k human judgments on real, cloned, and morphed voice pairs, testing model alignment with perceived identity rather than ground-truth speaker labels.
card.evaluation: Assessed 11 speech models on four tasks using Pearson correlation, AUC, and calibration metrics against listener majority responses and noise ceilings.
card.limitation: Models trained on metadata labels poorly predict human perception of synthetic voices, with no model reaching the noise ceiling.

slides.title: When Architectural Spaces Start to Act
slides.highlight: This paper explores how architectural robots reshape spatial conditions beyond immediate interactions, offering insights relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction within dynamic environments.

card.one_liner: Architectural robots shape inhabited spaces through persistent spatial configurations, not just motion, requiring new interaction paradigms.
card.key_idea: Interaction extends beyond robotic motion to the spatial conditions left behind, affecting occupant control, trust, and shared space negotiation.
card.evaluation: Reflective analysis drawing on prior studies (CHI/HRI) involving robotic partitions and benches; no new empirical data or baselines presented.
card.limitation: Lacks concrete technical solutions or quantitative metrics for managing multi-occupant conflicts and maintaining perceived control in dynamic spaces.

slides.title: A Framework for Task-Agnostic Counterfactual Fairness in Transformers through Activation Steering
slides.highlight: This work introduces MICF, a framework using mechanistic interpretability to enforce counterfactual fairness in transformers via activation steering, relevant to MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious hybrid human-AI societies by addressing bias in LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: MICF framework uses mechanistic interpretability and activation steering to enforce counterfactual fairness in transformers.
card.key_idea: Localizes sensitive attribute pathways via activation patching, then steers activations to mitigate bias without retraining or explicit causal models.
card.evaluation: Tested on UTICalc and COMPAS datasets using TabPFN; measured counterfactual fairness scores and accuracy with bootstrap confidence intervals.
card.limitation: Relies on LLM-generated counterfactuals and linear representation assumptions, which may be inaccurate under feature superposition or latent confounding.
